text:
Predicates:
Cost(x, y) ::: x costs y dollars.
Cheaper(x, y) ::: x is cheaper than y.
Provide(x, y, z) ::: x provides y to z.
FinancialAid(x) ::: x is financial aid.
GREApplicant(x) ::: x is a GRE applicant.
Prove(x, y) ::: x proves y.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x is economic hardship.
LiveIn(x, y) ::: x lives in y.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x is a single-parent family.
HaveFewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available to them.
Apply(x, y) ::: x is applying to take y.
Take(x, y) ::: x takes y.
Premises:
Cost(greTest, 205) ∧ Cheaper(205, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
∀x ((GREApplicant(x) ∧ Prove(x, economicHardship)) → Provide(ets, financialAid, x)) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x ((LiveIn(x, singleParentFamily) ∨ HaveFewResources(x)) → Prove(x, economicHardship)) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources available to them can prove economic hardship.
LiveIn(tom, singleParentFamily) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
HaveFewResources(tom) ::: Tom has few resources available to him.
Apply(tom, greTest) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
¬∃x ∃y (Take(x, greTest) ∧ Provide(y, financialAid, x)) ::: No one taking the GRE test has financial aid provided to them by something.
